mcqs.question: `CsvImporter` and `JsonImporter` each independently implement read-file, parse, validate, and save steps, with read-file and save duplicated verbatim between them. What's the maintenance risk?
options: A bug fix to the shared save logic must be applied in both classes, and a future importer isn't guaranteed to follow the same step order
The two classes will fail to compile because they share method names
CSV and JSON files cannot both be validated using the same programming language
Duplicated code always runs measurably slower than shared code
mcqs.explanation: The real risk is duplicated shared logic drifting out of sync (a fix applied to one copy but not the other) and no enforced structure guaranteeing every importer follows the same sequence. Shared method names across separate classes compile fine, format doesn't dictate language choice, and duplication isn't inherently a performance issue.

mcqs.question: Per the Hollywood Principle as applied in Template Method, who decides when a subclass's `parse()` method runs?
options: The base class's template method, which calls parse() at the specific point in its fixed sequence
The subclass itself, by calling parse() whenever it needs to
The client code that instantiated the subclass, on its own schedule
It runs automatically as soon as the subclass is constructed
mcqs.explanation: The Hollywood Principle inverts the usual control direction: the base class's template method calls the subclass's hook methods at points it decides, and the subclass never calls its own hooks or controls their timing. Client code only calls the one template method, and there's no automatic invocation at construction.

mcqs.question: A `ReportGenerator` object needs to swap its entire generation algorithm (PDF vs HTML vs plain-text) at runtime based on a user setting, not just override individual steps. Which pattern fits better?
options: Template Method, because it's the standard pattern for any algorithm with steps
Neither pattern applies to report generation
Strategy — the whole algorithm needs to be swappable at runtime, which inheritance-based Template Method can't do for an existing object
Template Method, since PDF/HTML/plain-text are just three subclasses of a fixed skeleton
mcqs.explanation: Template Method fixes an object's behavior at compile time via its class (a CsvImporter is always a CsvImporter); it can't swap which subclass an existing object behaves like at runtime. Strategy is built exactly for swapping an entire algorithm object at runtime, which is what a live user setting requires.

mcqs.question: A new `StreamingImporter` has to override `readFile()` to do something unrelated to reading a file, and effectively rewrites most of `DataImporter`'s template steps to work at all. What does this signal?
options: This is normal and expected — every new subclass typically overrides most of the base class
The base class needs to be marked final so no further subclasses can be added
DataImporter should be deleted entirely and replaced with a global function
The shared skeleton doesn't genuinely fit this case, and forcing it in defeats the point of Template Method — the skeleton needs redesigning or this case needs a different approach
mcqs.explanation: Overriding almost every step is a sign the shared sequence was never actually shared by this new case — the fix is to reconsider whether the skeleton should be redesigned or whether this case belongs to a different structure entirely, not to force-fit it. Marking the base class final or deleting it outright don't address the actual mismatch.
